modalLead: A fix-only release out of a sweep through the whole dashboard. The one worth knowing about: dragging a widget to reorder a page erased what its widgets were watching. Beside it, a closed tag cloud that went on swallowing clicks, a page that opened without its widgets if you hovered its tab first, and a kept pile that looked empty when a request failed.

items.text: Reordering a page no longer erases what its widgets watch. Dragging a widget dropped every list setting on that page — the disks a Disks tile listed, the figures Containers and Health showed, the tags Uptime and Neglected filtered by, and the names given to a disk.
A page opens with its widgets even when you hovered its tab on the way there. Hovering a page tab used to fetch it in a way that left the widgets and the block order behind.
A widget tile catches the light the way a panel in Config does. It was the one card-shaped surface that stayed matte on a theme with a sheen.
The tag cloud stops eating clicks when it closes. An invisible box the size of the cloud stayed over the grid, so bookmarks under it would not open and nothing said why.
A long category name fits again — shrunk a step at a time and wrapped to two lines, instead of cut off mid-word.
Move to… opens one popover, however fast the key repeats.
A collection rule names the category it offers instead of listing opaque ids.
The page name is in the browser tab from the first paint, instead of “Dashboard” until the scripts have run.

Shift + I opens the inbox on its first tab. It used to open on whichever tab you left it on, so it landed on Kept — and did nothing at all while you were already there. Shift + U is still the key that means Kept.
A failed reload leaves the kept pile on screen and says what happened, instead of drawing “Nothing kept yet.”
A preview the server refused is asked for again. Hovering a lot of rows at once meant those links never loaded a preview again.
The capture page answers in your language. The page a bookmarklet lands on was English whatever the install was set to.
A certificate about to expire reaches a webhook. Tick A TLS certificate is about to expire under Data & backups → Webhooks. It was already a notification and a browser push.
The Backups panel says where the backups are, and warns when that is inside the data directory they back up.
An uploaded icon no longer overwrites another one. Two bookmarks given different pictures with the same filename keep both, and a replaced icon actually appears.
